ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the outer contour is pentagon ABCDE, A is at the top, B and C are on the left side, E and D are on the right side, and CD is the bottom side. There are also two unlabeled interior points in the figure; denote the left interior point as P and the right interior point as Q. It can be directly seen that the drawn line segments include the outer sides AB, BC, CD, DE, EA, as well as the interior line segments AP, AQ, BQ, CQ, EP, DP, totaling 11. Reasoning: The problem states that the length of each line segment is 2. Therefore AB, AQ, BQ form equilateral triangle ABQ with side length 2; BC, CQ, BQ form equilateral triangle BCQ with side length 2; AE, AP, EP form equilateral triangle AEP with side length 2; DE, DP, EP form equilateral triangle DEP with side length 2. Triangles ABQ and BCQ share BQ, and A and C are located on the two sides of BQ, so ∠ABC = 60° + 60° = 120°, and AC = 2√3. Similarly, triangles AEP and DEP share EP, obtaining ∠AED = 120°, AD = 2√3. Connect AC and AD, dividing pentagon ABCDE into triangles ABC, ACD, ADE. The area of triangle ABC is (1/2)(2)(2)sin120° = √3, and the area of triangle ADE is likewise √3. The three sides of triangle ACD are AC = AD = 2√3, CD = 2; taking CD as the base, its height is √((2√3)^2 - 1^2) = √11, so the area is (1/2)(2)(√11) = √11. The total area is √3 + √11 + √3 = 2√3 + √11 = √12 + √11. Therefore m = 12, n = 11, m+n = 23.

method.method_draft: Synthetic equilateral-triangle decomposition. First name the two unlabeled interior points P on the left and Q on the right, as read from the image. The image shows segments AB, AQ, BQ; BC, CQ, BQ; AE, AP, EP; and DE, DP, EP. From the text, every drawn segment has length 2, so triangles ABQ, BCQ, AEP, and DEP are all equilateral. Thus in the left pair, A and C are opposite vertices of two equilateral triangles sharing BQ, so angle ABC = 120° and AC = 2√3. Similarly, angle AED = 120° and AD = 2√3. Draw diagonals AC and AD to split pentagon ABCDE into triangles ABC, ACD, and ADE. The two side triangles have area (1/2)(2)(2)sin120° = √3 each. Triangle ACD has sides 2√3, 2√3, and CD = 2; its height to CD is √((2√3)^2 - 1^2) = √11, so its area is √11. Therefore the pentagon area is 2√3 + √11 = √12 + √11, giving m+n = 12+11 = 23.

The three sides of triangle ACD are AC = AD = 2√3, CD = 2; taking CD as the base, its height is √((2√3)^2 - 1^2) = √11, so the area is (1/2)(2)(√11) = √11. The total area is √3 + √11 + √3 = 2√3 + √11 = √12 + √11. Therefore m = 12, n = 11, m+n = 23.
